title: Order-update stream status (NOT market-data health)
description: Source: src/box/orderStreamStatus.ts orderStreamStatus(). Answers one operator question: is the fast fill path running, or are fills observed by REST polling? A healthy market-data socket is NOT evidence of a working order-update stream: Zerodha sends order updates as TEXT frames on the same socket that carries binary ticks, and Dhan uses a separate order-update WebSocket. Carries no token, account id or secret.

any_stream_live.description: True only when at least one broker's order stream is genuinely delivering updates. False whenever fills depend on REST polling.

market_data_health_is_not_order_stream_h.description: Explicit anti-conflation flag. The UI MUST NOT present a healthy market-data feed as evidence that fills are observed promptly.

wiring.description: not_built = no implementation. not_wired = implemented and unit-tested but NO running component consumes it, so it cannot deliver a fill (this is NOT 'disabled by choice'). gated_off = wired but the env gate is not armed. armed = gate on; the health field then decides. not_applicable_paper = this deployment SIMULATES execution, so no order is sent to the broker and the broker has no order to report on; a paper process constructs no consumer BY DESIGN, because building one implies a live order manager and a paper process must contain no object capable of touching a real order. The absence of not_applicable_paper was itself a reporting defect: every paper deployment fell through to not_wired and so permanently reported a broken fast fill path that was never meant to exist. A client MUST render this as inactive / not applicable, NEVER as broken.

gate_env_var.description: Name of the env switch, so an operator can find it. NAME only, never a value.

lifecycle.description: SECTION 7. The AUTHORITATIVE order-stream lifecycle that decided fills_observed_by — the SAME value the live-entry gate scores. Null when nothing consumes the stream. Published here because defect (a) was precisely a lifecycle of DEGRADED sitting behind a health.state of LIVE and a fills_observed_by of stream_primary_rest_reconcile: the operator was shown the fast fill path at the moment entry was being refused for the opposite reason.

health.description: Live projection health, or null when nothing consumes the stream. `state` is DERIVED from `lifecycle` (see src/box/orderStreamConsumer.ts publishedStateForLifecycle), so the state that governs entry and the state the operator reads cannot disagree.

state.description: RECONNECTED_PENDING_RECONCILE mandates a REST reconciliation before the stream is trusted again; the gap must be repaired, never assumed empty. DEGRADED (SECTION 7) means connected but NOT delivering while a fill is expected — its absence was defect (a), because the state that is published had no way to express what the governing lifecycle could already reach. AUTH_EXPIRED (SECTION 7) is distinct from DOWN: reconnecting with a rejected credential is pointless.

lifecycle.description: The single lifecycle authority `state` was derived from, carried verbatim so a reader is never left inferring it.

fills_observed_by.description: The mechanism CURRENTLY responsible for observing a fill. rest_polling_only means fill-observation latency is bounded by the polling cadence and the pacing floor, not by broker push latency. simulated_paper_fills means the LOCAL execution simulator produces the fill against real streamed quotes: a broker cannot emit an order-update event for an order it never received, so reporting paper fills as rest_polling_only was not a conservative understatement but false, implying a broker round trip and a confirmation that do not exist. A client MUST render this as 'Simulated fills', never as 'REST polling only'.
